analysis:
Documentation-only change to docs/developer/build.md. Three additions at head: (1) lines 170-174 describe scripts/install-release-cmake.sh reusing a pre-unpacked CMake 3.31.12 under $RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE/cmake/3.31.12/universal when a universal.complete marker exists and the binary reports the exact version; otherwise it downloads and checksum-verifies the archive. (2) lines 273-277 say push runs request CI routing like same-repo PRs, and the plane's approval admits branches. (3) the new CI Caching section (lines 300-382) says only master/dev pushes save caches, PR caches are scoped to merge refs, checkouts set persist-credentials:false, and a fsck gate discards a corrupt .git cache.

No provider runtime, key custody, attestation, App Attest authorization (TB-011), WebSocket (TB-002) or other threat-model assets are touched. The changes concern CI/build tooling, and the threat model has no CI-runner trust boundary.

Security-relevant points are for the owners of the underlying scripts and workflows, not this doc diff:
- The CMake marker/version shortcut trusts the runner image's cache directory. The version check is not a checksum, so the real script should verify integrity or accept only image-controlled paths. The supplied evidence is only the doc patch, so this is an unverified contract, not a finding.
- Restricting cache saves to master/dev pushes, with persist-credentials:false and an fsck gate, reduces cache-poisoning risk from PRs. The doc describes these as mitigations; the workflow YAML is not supplied, so enforcement is unverified.
- Release, signing and publication jobs are stated to keep literal Blacksmith labels and to be unrouted. That is unchanged and not visible here.

No security regression is identified from the doc text. A later pass should check that ci.yml, provider-ci-build/action.yml and install-release-cmake.sh match these claims, particularly that release/signing paths never restore caches saved from untrusted refs and that push-triggered routing does not reach release lanes.
